learning_outcomes.text: Knowledge and capabilities for the calculation, design and testing of machines.

Ability to draft and develop projects in the field of mechanical engineering, for the construction, renovation, repair, conservation, demolition, manufacturing, installation, assembly or operation of: structures, mechanical equipment, energy installations, electrical installations, industrial installations and plants and manufacturing processes.
Ability to manage the activities subject to the engineering projects described in the previous section.
Ability to perform measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert opinions, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to handle specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Ability to interpret technical projects and reports.
Ability to evaluate the effectiveness, viability and quality of the implemented solutions.
Demonstrate the ability to analyze and synthesize.
Acquire the ability to solve problems effectively.
Possess the ability to make decisions.
Ability to apply knowledge to practice.
Acquire the capacity for autonomous learning and concern for knowledge and lifelong learning.
Understand and evaluate the different forms of mechanical element failure, as well as the theories commonly used in mechanical design, both for static and dynamic failure.
Be able to apply this knowledge to the design, calculation or selection of the main machine elements.

teaching_methods: Theoretical classes (Lectures with multimedia projector and/or whiteboard)
Practical classes (Problem-solving and practical case resolution in small groups)
Tutorials (Individual or small group academic tutorials to resolve doubts, questions and problems, available in-person, by e-mail and videoconference)

assessment_methods.method: Completion of problems, exercises, work, etc. during classes, distributed throughout the semester

assessment_rules: A minimum score of 4 out of 10 points is required for the theoretical-practical written test and the global practical problems test. A minimum score of 3 out of 10 points is required for the set of in-class problems, exercises, and work. If any of these minimums are not met, the overall course grade will be calculated according to the UBU Evaluation Regulations. The evaluation system for exchange students may be modified if the academic calendars of the home and host universities do not coincide. For exceptional evaluation, there will be a theoretical-practical test (30%), a problems test (40%), and a personal project (30%).
